question: What tariffs did the US announce on 'Liberation Day' in April 2025?
text:
On **April 2, 2025**, which President Donald Trump called **“Liberation Day,”** the U.S. announced two tiers of new import tariffs under Executive Order 14257: ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/04/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-declares-national-emergency-to-increase-our-competitive-edge-protect-our-sovereignty-and-strengthen-our-national-and-economic-security/?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block&utm_source=openai))

- **A 10% baseline tariff** on most U.S. imports, effective **April 5, 2025**. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/regulating-imports-with-a-reciprocal-tariff-to-rectify-trade-practices-that-contribute-to-large-and-persistent-annual-united-states-goods-trade-deficits/?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))
- **Higher “reciprocal” tariffs** for dozens of trading partners, scheduled for **April 9, 2025**. These rates would **replace** the 10% baseline, not stack on top of it. The announced rates included **20% for the European Union, 24% for Japan, 25% for South Korea, 26% for India, 32% for Taiwan, 34% for China, 46% for Vietnam, 49% for Cambodia, and 50% for Lesotho**. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/04/regulating-imports-with-a-reciprocal-tariff-to-rectify-trade-practices-that-contribute-to-large-and-persistent-annual-united-states-goods-trade-deficits/?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))

**Canada and Mexico** stayed under separate tariff rules. The new tariffs also excluded certain goods, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and energy products, as well as steel, aluminum, and autos already covered by separate sectoral tariffs. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/04/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-declares-national-emergency-to-increase-our-competitive-edge-protect-our-sovereignty-and-strengthen-our-national-and-economic-security/?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block&utm_source=openai))

These were the **originally announced rates**. On **April 9**, the administration announced a 90-day pause on most of the higher rates, effective **April 10**, leaving the 10% baseline in place for most partners while raising the rate on China. ([everycrsreport.com](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R48549.html?utm_source=openai))
